import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 274

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
* [arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
* [arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
* [PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
* [arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
-/

open scoped Pointwise Cardinal

namespace Erdos274

-- TODO(callesonne): add already proved results from the wiki page

/-- An exact covering of a group `G` is a finite collection of subgroups `{H_1, ..., H_k}` and
representative `{g_1, ..., g_k}` such that the cosets `g_iH_i` are pairwise disjoint and their
union covers `G`.

Note that this differs from `Partition (α := Subgroup G)` because the covering condition there
invokes `Subgroup.sup` which is subgroup generation and thus stronger than union. This definition
is easier to use in this context than the alternative `Partition (α := Set G)`, which lacks
subgroup definitions such as `Subgroup.index`. -/
structure Group.ExactCovering (G : Type*) [Group G] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] where
  parts : ι → Subgroup G
  reps : ι → G
  nonempty (i : ι) : (parts i : Set G).Nonempty
  disjoint : (Set.univ (α := ι)).PairwiseDisjoint fun (i : ι) ↦ reps i • (parts i : Set G)
  covers : ⋃ i, reps i • (parts i : Set G) = Set.univ

/--
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι],
    ∀ (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι →
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jostamon/erdos274-hs-abelian/blob/2ab8a2e39e7dd7836adf577b52555f069244466f/Erdos274/Main.lean"]
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G]
    (hG : 1 < Fintype.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι)
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by
  sorry

end Erdos274

findings.description: The yes/no answer has reversed polarity. Lines 60–63 put the universal assertion that every nontrivial exact covering has two equal-sized parts on the RHS of `answer(sorry) ↔`. The source asks whether an exact covering with pairwise distinct coset sizes exists. If Q denotes that existence assertion, the current RHS is equivalent to ¬Q, not Q. Thus `answer(True)` would encode the source's negative answer, and `answer(False)` its positive answer. The universal non-existence assertion is a legitimate conjecture, but the answer slot as written answers the opposite question. In `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, `main_rhs_iff_neg_source` proves this equivalence and `cannot_use_same_answer` proves that the two formulations cannot use the same answer; neither proof depends on `sorryAx`.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős Problem 274 asks: “If $G$ is a group then can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets)”. Its remarks explicitly say that for abelian G “the answer to the original question is no.” Source: https://www.erdosproblems.com/274, read through the archived snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20260528171645id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/274.
findings.suggested_fix: Negate the entire current universal RHS: `answer(sorry) ↔ ¬ (∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], 1 < ENat.card G → ∀ (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι), 1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j))`. Equivalently, use an existential formulation asserting a nontrivial finite exact covering whose part-cardinality function is injective.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the natural-number-valued `Subgroup.index`, which returns zero for infinite index, without explicitly assuming finite indices. It also adds `1 < ENat.card G`, absent from the source's general statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both differences are harmless. By the B. H. Neumann finite-cover theorem, the finite-index cosets alone cover G. Every coset in an exact covering is nonempty and disjoint from every other one, so none can be omitted; hence every part has finite index. Therefore `Subgroup.index` is the genuine finite index, and its zero default is unreachable. Furthermore, more than one disjoint nonempty coset forces G to be nontrivial, so the extra hypothesis follows from the others. The scratch file proves these facts and `herzog_source_equivalence`, an explicit ↔ between the Lean formulation and the version with genuine quotient cardinalities and no extra group-size hypothesis.

review.notes:
All declarations were checked. Boundary experiments rule out empty-index coverings and nontrivial coverings of the trivial group, and construct a two-part covering of the cyclic group of order two. Coset and subgroup cardinalities agree. Cardinality versus index is not an additional defect: they determine each other for finite groups; for infinite groups every part of a finite exact covering has cardinality #G. The cited finite-normal-core quotient reduction relates the universal cardinality and index conjectures.

The finite abelian formal-proof record was verified. Its dependency chain and Main theorem compile in a scratch copy with only an additional GeomSum import needed for the newer installed Mathlib. `/workspace/review/abelian_bridge.lean` translates the external covering structure to the file's structure and proves the exact FC statement. Its axioms, and those of the linked Main theorem, are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

The live Erdős page returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive user agents. Its archived mathematical statement was read in full; the current linked community database still records problem 274 as open. The other sources support the open general case and solved abelian case. The reviewed file's hash matches the specified commit.

not_demonstrated.reason: Reversing the yes/no answer polarity does not trivialize the universal coset-partition assertion. I have no short independent proof or disproof of the declaration as stated. The scratch equivalence with the negation of the source's existence question demonstrates the polarity contrast, but does not satisfy this task's requirement to prove or refute the actual declaration.

submission.summary: No qualifying trivial proof or disproof was found. No trivial_proof.lean file was created or left behind, and no compilation was attempted.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported issue concerns answer polarity, not an elementary counterexample or a vacuous hypothesis. Proving the actual universal assertion would resolve the underlying open conjecture; proving only the logical polarity comparison would not meet the requested demonstration criteria.

submission.summary: Negated the entire universal RHS of `erdos_274`, correcting the answer polarity to match the source’s existence question. No other declarations, docstrings, references, or attributes were changed. The edited file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
